headline: Highest risk is data leakage from shared workspace: Notion AI can read workspace pages while pdf.js processes PDFs in-browser, creating a plausible cross-agent exposure path; prompt injection and capability conflict are lower.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A can ingest workspace pages and team knowledge base content, while B processes PDF files in a browser. If B’s PDFs are imported into the shared workspace or copied into pages, malicious PDF text can influence A’s RAG-style responses. The shared workspace state makes the bridge plausible, though not proven by docs.
conditions: IF PDF content is copied into Notion pages or databases
IF A is prompted to summarize or act on B-produced document text without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a provenance banner to imported PDFs before summarization
Review B outputs before pasting into A
Use a separate workspace for untrusted PDFs
Disable auto-summarization of newly imported documents

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches workspace pages and team knowledge base content and uses vendor backends; B touches PDF documents locally in a browser. Because A has shared workspace state across instances, sensitive PDF-derived content can flow into A’s outputs if documents are moved into the workspace, creating a realistic leakage path. B’s lack of network egress lowers but does not remove the risk.
conditions: IF PDF documents contain sensitive data and are imported into the shared workspace
IF A is used to summarize or answer questions about those documents
mitigations: Keep sensitive PDFs outside the shared workspace
Restrict A to a separate Notion workspace
Redact PDFs before import
Limit sharing permissions on pages containing PDF extracts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or execute shell commands, while B only runs browsers and has no network egress. Their write surfaces do not overlap in the profiles, so direct resource contention is limited. The only plausible conflict is shared workspace state, which is narrower than the rubric’s medium/high indicators.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same shared workspace pages
IF B’s browser workflow mutates documents that A also edits
mitigations: Assign separate pages to each agent
Use read-only access for B
Serialize edits manually
Snapshot pages before concurrent work

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, and B is a browser-based PDF processor. If B’s extracted text is pasted into the workspace, A may treat it as authoritative and generate downstream answers from it without verification. That creates a default-path cascade from B into A, though no direct action-taking authority is shown.
conditions: IF B-produced PDF text is imported into pages A can read
IF A’s answers are used without human verification
mitigations: Require source links in A outputs
Cross-check A answers against original PDFs
Mark imported text as untrusted
Add a human review step before acting on A outputs

E_compliance.rationale: A is vendor-hosted and sends content to vendor backends, while B is open-source browser-based PDF processing with no network egress. The profiles do not show a specific residency or certification mismatch, so only a general compliance gap exists: sensitive workspace content may leave the local environment when A is used. B is not cited for residency because none is stated.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Notion pages
IF the organization requires local-only processing for that data class
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from A
Use a local-only workflow for PDFs
Document data-handling boundaries
Review vendor terms before enabling A on sensitive pages
